item.title: Mac mini M4 16 GB: Measured Ollama Speed and Memory for Qwen3.5 4B and 9B
item.description:
Affiliate disclosure: Some links are affiliate links. As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases. See Disclosure.

This page holds numbers I measured on my own desk machine, not estimates. If a model or a Mac is not in the table, I have not tested it, and I would rather leave the cell out than guess.

The machine and the method

  • Hardware: Mac mini (2024), Apple M4, 16 GB unified memory. Apple lists the base M4 at 120 GB/s memory bandwidth and the M4 Pro at 273 GB/s (Apple tech specs).
  • Runtime: Ollama 0.40.7; the models are the stock qwen3.5:4b (4.0 GB on disk) and qwen3.5:9b (7.6 GB on disk) tags.
  • Run: 2 November 2026, 12:15 to 12:18 IST. One 35-token prompt, 256 tokens max output, temperature 0.2, thinking disabled, three runs per model at num_ctx 4096 and 8192. Other desk services were idle, with about 78% of memory free before the first run.
  • What I report: generation speed from Ollama’s own eval_count / eval_duration, and resident size from /api/ps. I do not report prompt-processing speed, because the repeated prompt was cached and the figures are meaningless.

Results

Model num_ctx Gen tok/s (3 runs) Resident memory (GB, /api/ps)
qwen3.5:4b 4096 18.4 (cold), 22.4, 22.5 4.1 to 4.3
qwen3.5:4b 8192 21.1, 23.2, 23.5 4.3 to 4.4
qwen3.5:9b 4096 19.4, 19.4, 19.2 7.8 to 7.9
qwen3.5:9b 8192 19.2, 19.3, 17.8 8.0 to 8.1

Cold-load time was 6.3 s for the 4B model and 10.1 s for the 9B model from the internal SSD.

The imperative for disclosure has moved beyond voluntary best practice into a realm of regulatory and platform-enforced necessity. Major content hosts, including YouTube, TikTok, and various social feed aggregators, now enforce mandatory labeling for AI-generated audio. These mandates are designed to prevent deception; listeners must be able to distinguish between a human speaker and a synthetic voice before consuming the content. While some jurisdictions are still drafting specific legislation regarding deepfakes and synthetic media, the operational reality is that non-compliance can lead to content removal or account restrictions.

1. Why a UI layer (and when the CLI is enough)

The command line works well if you are comfortable typing prompts and managing tokens manually. If you only need to chat with one model or run a simple script, the terminal is sufficient.
